name: gnosis-vpn
title: Gnosis VPN
description: Who uses Gnosis VPN, how much traffic it carries and where, read from the HOPR network’s on-chain ticket redemptions.

lists.name: exits
lists.description: Exit node addresses, per data source. Downstream volume counts only the exits listed here.

queries.title: Event logs
queries.description: Fragment: every stored log of the given events, by signature hash — the raw rows Blokli keeps in `log`, less those a reorg removed. FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\x…'::bytea])}} AS e.
queries.sql:
-- Every stored log of the given events, by signature hash: the raw rows
-- Blokli keeps in `log` for the contracts it watches, less those a reorg
-- removed. The other fragments read the chain through this one.
--
--   FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\x004c…'::bytea, '\xed22…'::bytea])}} AS e
--
-- `topics` is the event's topics concatenated, 32 bytes each, the signature
-- first; an indexed address is the last 20 bytes of its topic. `data` is the
-- ABI encoding of the arguments that are not indexed, a 32-byte word each.
--
-- Blokli indexes `log` by position only, so this reads the whole table; an
-- index on SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) would let it read only the events
-- asked for.
SELECT block_number, tx_index, log_index, address, topics, data
FROM log
WHERE removed = FALSE
  AND SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = ANY ({{$signatures = ARRAY['\x004c0177ad15bb302b4419e9ac96065d6f436e0f61972f97bbe272834c40f934'::bytea]}})

queries.title: Key bindings
queries.description: Fragment: every account — a chain key bound to a packet key — once, at its first KeyBinding event, with its key id.
queries.sql:
-- Every account: a chain key bound to a packet key, once, at its first
-- binding, where Blokli creates the account (the key id is its account id).
--
-- The Announcements contract's KeyBinding(bytes32 ed25519_sig_0,
-- bytes32 ed25519_sig_1, bytes32 ed25519_pub_key, address chain_key,
-- uint256 key_id) indexes nothing: the chain key is the last 20 bytes of data
-- word 3, the key id word 4. Blokli refuses a key id above 2³²−1, and so does
-- this; it also verifies the binding's ed25519 signature, which SQL cannot.
SELECT DISTINCT ON (chain_key)
  chain_key,
  key_id,
  block_number,
  tx_index,
  log_index
FROM (
  SELECT
    SUBSTRING(data FROM 109 FOR 20) AS chain_key,
    ('x' || encode(SUBSTRING(data FROM 157 FOR 4), 'hex'))::bit(32)::bigint AS key_id,
    block_number,
    tx_index,
    log_index
  FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\x11d94653de52fc143887956fe4b5e4120a850b1300ece0533dee6bd8ff91f732'::bytea])}} AS e
  WHERE OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 160
    AND SUBSTRING(data FROM 129 FOR 28) = decode(repeat('00', 28), 'hex')
) AS binding
ORDER BY chain_key, block_number, tx_index, log_index

queries.title: VPN nodes
queries.description: Fragment: every announced node (relays and exits), by address, from the announcement events.
queries.sql:
-- The network's infrastructure, relays and exits alike: every account whose
-- latest announcement stands. Announcements do not tell relays from exits; the
-- exits are told by the service registry (registry-entries) and the list
-- "exits" (Settings → Lists).
--
-- The Announcements contract's AddressAnnouncement(address node,
-- string baseMultiaddr) announces and RevokeAnnouncement(address node)
-- withdraws every announcement before it. Neither indexes its arguments, so
-- the node is data word 0. An empty address is skipped, as Blokli skips it:
-- its encoding is then three words, no more. Only accounts count.
WITH account AS MATERIALIZED {{> key-bindings}}
SELECT announced.node AS address
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (node) node, revoked
  FROM (
    SELECT
      SUBSTRING(data FROM 13 FOR 20) AS node,
      SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = '\xa4de30a528becadf82649d1395c0e30dd18ae35b5a96ce71e9295bb14bc9f3bc'::bytea AS revoked,
      block_number,
      tx_index,
      log_index
    FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\xc4df5ba16814838ab2618829d68f8623bb897302f24dbdba2279dbe45adb3d14'::bytea, '\xa4de30a528becadf82649d1395c0e30dd18ae35b5a96ce71e9295bb14bc9f3bc'::bytea])}} AS e
    WHERE OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 32
      AND (SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = '\xa4de30a528becadf82649d1395c0e30dd18ae35b5a96ce71e9295bb14bc9f3bc'::bytea OR OCTET_LENGTH(data) > 96)
  ) AS event
  ORDER BY node, block_number DESC, tx_index DESC, log_index DESC
) AS announced
WHERE NOT announced.revoked
  AND announced.node IN (SELECT chain_key FROM account)

queries.title: VPN clients
queries.description: Fragment: every account that is not an announced node — the VPN clients — with the block it was deployed in.
queries.sql:
-- VPN clients: accounts that bound a key but are not announced nodes, so
-- they are not infrastructure. An account starts with its key binding, so
-- that block is when the client was deployed.
SELECT
  account.key_id AS account_id,
  account.chain_key AS client,
  account.block_number AS deployed_block
FROM {{> key-bindings}} AS account
WHERE account.chain_key NOT IN (SELECT address FROM {{> vpn-nodes}} AS node)

queries.title: Registered exits
queries.description: The gvpn:exit entries standing in the service registry.
queries.sql:
-- The Gnosis VPN exits the service registry lists: one row per registered
-- gvpn:exit entry that stands. The exit is the registered node: its address
-- is what pays relays for the return path.
--
-- The HoprServiceRegistry emits Registered and Updated as
-- (bytes32 indexed serviceType, address indexed node, address indexed safe,
-- bytes metadata, uint48 registeredAt, uint256 burned) and Deregistered as
-- (bytes32 indexed serviceType, address indexed node, address indexed safe).
-- The topics hold the type (topic 1), the node (2) and the safe (3); the data
-- is the offset of the metadata, two words, then its length and its bytes.
-- An entry stands from its latest event on: Updated replaces the metadata,
-- Deregistered ends it. The service type is its name right-padded with zeros,
-- here 'gvpn:exit'.
--
-- The metadata of a gvpn:exit entry is a JSON object that says where the exit
-- is reached, for example
--
--   {"version": 1, "gnosis_vpn_server": "host:8000",
--    "wireguard_server": "host:51820", "meta": {"name": "GVPN-KR-1"}}
--
-- The fields are picked out by pattern, so a malformed object, or one without
-- a field, costs that field and not the entry.
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (node) node, safe, deregistered, metadata
  FROM (
    SELECT
      SUBSTRING(topics FROM 77 FOR 20) AS node,
      SUBSTRING(topics FROM 109 FOR 20) AS safe,
      SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = '\xc156047b6a581b0578bc0cf242ee21ab84be919cf764ffd68ce50ded302323a7'::bytea AS deregistered,
      CASE
        WHEN OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 128 THEN SUBSTRING(
          data FROM 129
          FOR LEAST(('x' || encode(SUBSTRING(data FROM 125 FOR 4), 'hex'))::bit(32)::bigint, 2048)::int
        )
      END AS metadata,
      block_number,
      tx_index,
      log_index
    FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\x113517b01f8948e66b44bc59b45e47477fb89b357e7d1939b0d211dd15b698fe'::bytea, '\xd290c349227ff04b271178af5d66f5375b072d8acfecd2ffcc80ec7ea77c69f5'::bytea, '\xc156047b6a581b0578bc0cf242ee21ab84be919cf764ffd68ce50ded302323a7'::bytea])}} AS e
    WHERE OCTET_LENGTH(topics) >= 128
      AND SUBSTRING(topics FROM 33 FOR 32) = decode(rpad(encode('gvpn:exit'::bytea, 'hex'), 64, '0'), 'hex')
  ) AS event
  ORDER BY node, block_number DESC, tx_index DESC, log_index DESC
),
described AS (
  SELECT node, safe, encode(metadata, 'escape') AS metadata
  FROM latest
  WHERE NOT deregistered
)
SELECT
  node AS address,
  safe,
  (regexp_match(metadata, '"name"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"'))[1] AS name,
  (regexp_match(metadata, '"gnosis_vpn_server"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"'))[1] AS vpn_server,
  (regexp_match(metadata, '"wireguard_server"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"'))[1] AS wireguard_server,
  metadata
FROM described

queries.title: Exit addresses
queries.description: The exits: registered ones plus those listed by hand.
queries.sql:
-- The addresses of the network's Gnosis VPN exits: those the service registry
-- lists as gvpn:exit (registry-entries, each a registered node) together with those added by hand to
-- the list "exits" (Settings → Lists). The registry makes the list optional:
-- on a network that has one, exits appear and disappear as they register and
-- deregister; the list is for a network without a registry, or an exit that
-- is not in it. With neither, no address is returned and nothing is counted
-- as downstream.
--
-- One row per address; `in_registry` and `in_list` say where it was found.
SELECT
  address,
  BOOL_OR(origin = 'registry') AS in_registry,
  BOOL_OR(origin = 'list') AS in_list
FROM (
  SELECT address, 'registry' AS origin
  FROM {{> registry-entries}} AS entry
    UNION ALL
  SELECT address, 'list' AS origin
  FROM unnest({{list:exits}}) AS listed (address)
) AS found
GROUP BY address

queries.title: Channel events
queries.description: Fragment: every event on a payment channel, decoded — the channel's ends, and its status, epoch, ticket index and balance after the event.
queries.sql:
-- Every event on a payment channel, decoded: the channel's two ends and its
-- state after the event.
--
-- The Channels contract's ChannelOpened, ChannelBalanceIncreased and
-- ChannelBalanceDecreased, TicketRedeemed, OutgoingChannelClosureInitiated
-- and ChannelClosed each index the channel id (topic 1) and carry the whole
-- channel, packed into one 32-byte word:
--
--   bytes 0-5 padding · 6 status · 7-9 epoch · 10-13 closure time ·
--   14-19 ticket index · 20-31 balance (wei)
--
-- Status is 0 closed, 1 open, 2 closure initiated. Only ChannelOpened names
-- the ends, as topics 2 (source, the payer) and 3 (destination), so every
-- event takes them from its channel's opening, by a window over the channel
-- rather than a join: the planner cannot estimate how many rows a byte
-- pattern matches, and would run a join as a nested loop over the whole log.
--
-- Blokli records a channel only between two accounts, and marks an event on a
-- channel it never saw opened as corrupted; both are left out here.
WITH account AS MATERIALIZED {{> key-bindings}}
SELECT
  channel_id,
  SUBSTRING(ends FROM 13 FOR 20) AS source,
  SUBSTRING(ends FROM 45 FOR 20) AS destination,
  event,
  block_number,
  tx_index,
  log_index,
  status,
  epoch,
  closure_time,
  ticket_index,
  balance
FROM (
  SELECT
    decoded.*,
    FIRST_VALUE(opening) OVER channel AS ends
  FROM (
    SELECT
      SUBSTRING(topics FROM 33 FOR 32) AS channel_id,
      CASE SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32)
        WHEN '\x004c0177ad15bb302b4419e9ac96065d6f436e0f61972f97bbe272834c40f934'::bytea THEN 'opened'
        WHEN '\xec21547ca1e22edc3f9b4f4e0da94638b5b94dcb18d52dcc072abe5801a8013c'::bytea THEN 'balance-increased'
        WHEN '\x0c4672f14b63bb6354fac475ee498055a2784455673af224717b9770fd68d8d1'::bytea THEN 'balance-decreased'
        WHEN '\xed22f34d154d253a7f6fd477439be59080a1554aa0d0642686d64223ab544c8a'::bytea THEN 'ticket-redeemed'
        WHEN '\x0061e8037197b4d91cf8add2a0736613459081f236d1c8ab58549ebbc330b4e3'::bytea THEN 'closure-initiated'
        ELSE 'closed'
      END AS event,
      -- An opening between two accounts: its topics 2 and 3.
      CASE
        WHEN SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = '\x004c0177ad15bb302b4419e9ac96065d6f436e0f61972f97bbe272834c40f934'::bytea
          AND OCTET_LENGTH(topics) >= 128
          AND SUBSTRING(topics FROM 77 FOR 20) IN (SELECT chain_key FROM account)
          AND SUBSTRING(topics FROM 109 FOR 20) IN (SELECT chain_key FROM account)
          THEN SUBSTRING(topics FROM 65 FOR 64)
      END AS opening,
      block_number,
      tx_index,
      log_index,
      GET_BYTE(data, 6) AS status,
      ('x' || encode(SUBSTRING(data FROM 8 FOR 3), 'hex'))::bit(24)::bigint AS epoch,
      ('x' || encode(SUBSTRING(data FROM 11 FOR 4), 'hex'))::bit(32)::bigint AS closure_time,
      ('x' || encode(SUBSTRING(data FROM 15 FOR 6), 'hex'))::bit(48)::bigint AS ticket_index,
      SUBSTRING(data FROM 21 FOR 12) AS balance
    FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\x004c0177ad15bb302b4419e9ac96065d6f436e0f61972f97bbe272834c40f934'::bytea, '\xec21547ca1e22edc3f9b4f4e0da94638b5b94dcb18d52dcc072abe5801a8013c'::bytea, '\x0c4672f14b63bb6354fac475ee498055a2784455673af224717b9770fd68d8d1'::bytea, '\xed22f34d154d253a7f6fd477439be59080a1554aa0d0642686d64223ab544c8a'::bytea, '\x0061e8037197b4d91cf8add2a0736613459081f236d1c8ab58549ebbc330b4e3'::bytea, '\x197bba684a6afb7ba24f1d265605414b1d0051a6e295d6ff7b6e78e870d7a7f0'::bytea])}} AS e
    WHERE OCTET_LENGTH(topics) >= 64
      AND OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 32
  ) AS decoded
  WINDOW channel AS (
    PARTITION BY channel_id
    ORDER BY opening IS NULL, block_number, tx_index, log_index
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  )
) AS event
WHERE ends IS NOT NULL

queries.title: VPN redemptions
queries.description: Fragment: every ticket redemption that carried VPN traffic, upstream or downstream, with its block and tickets.
queries.sql:
-- Ticket redemptions that carried Gnosis VPN traffic, one row each.
--
-- Every channel event carries the channel's ticket index, and only a
-- redemption advances it: an event whose index is above the previous event's,
-- in the same epoch, marks a redemption on that channel. The jump is not the
-- tickets redeemed: a client numbers a ticket for every packet and only
-- winners are redeemed, so it estimates the packets paid for.
--
-- Payment follows the sender of each hop and a packet's destination is never
-- paid, so one VPN session leaves two paid hops on chain:
--
--   upstream     a client — an account that never announced — paying a relay
--   downstream   one of the network's configured exits paying a relay for
--                the answer
--
-- Everything else on these channels is announced nodes probing each other,
-- and is left out. The exits are those the service registry lists as gvpn:exit
-- and those in the list "exits" (exit-addresses); neither means no downstream
-- at all rather than a guess.
--
-- The qualifying channels are picked FIRST, so the window function runs over
-- their events only: every predicate is a property of the channel, and the
-- window partitions by channel, so dropping a channel cannot change the LAG of
-- a row that survives.
WITH node AS MATERIALIZED {{> vpn-nodes}},
exit_node AS MATERIALIZED {{> exit-addresses}},
vpn_event AS (
  SELECT
    e.*,
    CASE
      WHEN e.source NOT IN (SELECT address FROM node) THEN 'upstream'
      ELSE 'downstream'
    END AS direction
  FROM {{> channel-events}} AS e
  WHERE e.destination IN (SELECT address FROM node)
    AND (
      e.source NOT IN (SELECT address FROM node)
      OR e.source IN (SELECT address FROM exit_node)
    )
),
ordered AS (
  SELECT
    direction,
    source AS payer,
    destination AS relay,
    channel_id,
    block_number,
    tx_index,
    log_index,
    epoch,
    ticket_index,
    LAG(epoch) OVER w AS previous_epoch,
    LAG(ticket_index) OVER w AS previous_ticket_index
  FROM vpn_event
  WINDOW w AS (
    PARTITION BY channel_id
    ORDER BY block_number, tx_index, log_index
  )
)
SELECT
  direction,
  payer,
  relay,
  encode(channel_id, 'hex') AS channel,
  block_number AS block,
  tx_index,
  log_index,
  ticket_index - previous_ticket_index AS tickets
FROM ordered
WHERE previous_ticket_index IS NOT NULL
  AND epoch = previous_epoch
  AND ticket_index > previous_ticket_index

queries.title: Hex
queries.description: Expression fragment: bytes as a 0x-prefixed hex string. {{> hex(address)}}.
queries.sql:
-- Bytes as 0x-prefixed hex text, the way addresses are read everywhere.
--
--   {{> hex(account.chain_key)}}   →   '0x6b3c…'
'0x' || encode({{$value = '\x00ff'::bytea}}, 'hex')

queries.title: Indexed block
queries.description: Expression fragment: the last block the index has read — the head every block window counts back from.
queries.sql:
-- The last block the index has read: the head of the chain as far as these
-- dashboards know, and where every "last N blocks" window ends. Results carry
-- it as `head_block`.
--
-- The one value read from Blokli's bookkeeping rather than the event log. An
-- index that keeps only the log would read its own cursor here, or
-- (SELECT MAX(block_number) FROM log), which lags while the chain is quiet.
(SELECT last_indexed_block FROM chain_info ORDER BY id LIMIT 1)

queries.title: Client activity
queries.description: Each block in which each client was active — redeemed for or deployed — with its deployment block.
queries.sql:
-- Each block in which each VPN client was active, with its deployment block.
--
-- A client (vpn-clients) is active in a block when a relay redeemed one of its
-- tickets there, or when it was deployed there — so a new client counts at
-- once rather than only after its first redemption. One row per client and
-- block:
--
--   kind            `deployed` in its deployment block, `redeemed` otherwise
--   redemptions     0 in a deployment block with no traffic
--   deployed_block  the client's deployment block, on every row
--   head_block      the last block indexed
--
-- Feeds the active-client counts and the deployment cohorts.
WITH deployment AS (
  SELECT client, deployed_block FROM {{> vpn-clients}} AS clients
),
redeemed AS (
  SELECT r.payer AS client, r.block, COUNT(*) AS redemptions
  FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
  WHERE r.direction = 'upstream'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
active AS (
  SELECT client, block, redemptions FROM redeemed
  UNION ALL
  SELECT client, deployed_block, 0 FROM deployment
)
SELECT
  {{> hex(active.client)}} AS client,
  active.block,
  deployment.deployed_block,
  CASE WHEN active.block = deployment.deployed_block THEN 'deployed' ELSE 'redeemed' END AS kind,
  SUM(active.redemptions)::integer AS redemptions,
  {{> indexed-block}} AS head_block
FROM active
LEFT JOIN deployment ON deployment.client = active.client
GROUP BY active.client, active.block, deployment.deployed_block
ORDER BY active.block, client

queries.title: Decode winning probability
queries.description: Expression fragment: the 7-byte encoded winning probability as a number between 0 and 1.
queries.sql:
-- HOPR's 7-byte winning probability as a number from 0 to 1.
--
-- As hopr-types' WinningProbability::as_f64 does it: read big-endian, add
-- one, and keep the top 52 bits as the mantissa of a float in [1, 2), less
-- one. That is ((v + 1) >> 4) / 2^52 — exact in double precision, and 0 and 1
-- for the all-zero and all-ones encodings.
--
--   {{> decode-win-prob(value)}}   →   0.2
((('x' || encode({{$value = '\xffffffffffffff'::bytea}}, 'hex'))::bit(56)::bigint + 1) >> 4)::float8
  / 4503599627370496

queries.title: Oracle updates
queries.description: Fragment: every winning-probability and ticket-price update from the oracle events, raw value and position.
queries.sql:
-- Every update of the two oracle values the dashboard prices traffic with,
-- oldest first: `ticket-price` (value: the new price, 32 bytes, in wei) and
-- `win-prob` (value: the new winning probability, 7 bytes; decode it with
-- decode-win-prob).
--
--   TicketPriceUpdated(uint256,uint256)  d4c5e06b…f3fb
--   WinProbUpdated(uint56,uint56)        02728c4a…3800
--
-- Neither event indexes its arguments, so data word 1 is the new value: the
-- price is the whole word, at offset 33; a uint56 is right-aligned in its
-- word, so the probability is its last 7 bytes, at offset 58.
SELECT
  block_number,
  tx_index,
  log_index,
  CASE
    WHEN SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3800'::bytea THEN 'win-prob'
    ELSE 'ticket-price'
  END AS kind,
  CASE
    WHEN SUBSTRING(topics FROM 1 FOR 32) = '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3800'::bytea THEN SUBSTRING(data FROM 58 FOR 7)
    ELSE SUBSTRING(data FROM 33 FOR 32)
  END AS value
FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\xd4c5e06b1ae097ba02372652a7adaa6e4a8e00be527497a3ad0ebc3f761ef3fb'::bytea, '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3800'::bytea])}} AS e
WHERE OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 64
ORDER BY block_number, tx_index, log_index

queries.title: Winning probability history
queries.description: Fragment: the winning probability in force over each range of blocks, from the oracle logs.
queries.sql:
-- The winning probability in force over each range of blocks.
--
-- Each update in oracle-updates holds from its block until the next one's.
-- Blocks before the first update have no probability on record: they match no
-- row here, and the queries that join this price them at zero rather than
-- guess.
SELECT
  block_number AS from_block,
  COALESCE(
    LEAD(block_number) OVER (ORDER BY block_number, tx_index, log_index),
    9223372036854775807
  ) AS to_block,
  {{> decode-win-prob(value)}} AS probability
FROM {{> oracle-updates}} AS oracle
WHERE kind = 'win-prob'

queries.title: VPN traffic
queries.description: Every VPN redemption, by block, with its direction, payer, relay and data volume.
queries.sql:
-- Every Gnosis VPN redemption, by block, converted to data volume.
--
-- One row per redemption from vpn-redemptions: upstream (a client paying a
-- relay) and downstream (a configured exit paying a relay for the answer).
-- Most of the dashboard is drawn from this one result: volume, redemptions,
-- the relay breakdowns, the client ranking and each client's own record.
--
-- Volume: a redemption pays for one winning ticket, and with winning
-- probability p a winner stands for 1/p tickets of 650 bytes each, so it
-- accounts for 650 / (2^30 × p) GB at the p in force at its block. Before the
-- oracle's first update p is unknown, and the redemption counts with no volume.
--
-- Time is the block number. The event log keeps no block times, and a time
-- estimated from block counts drifts, so none is given. `head_block`, the last
-- block indexed, is where the dashboard's "last N blocks" windows end.
SELECT
  r.block,
  {{> indexed-block}} AS head_block,
  r.direction,
  {{> hex(r.payer)}} AS payer,
  {{> hex(r.relay)}} AS relay,
  r.tickets,
  COALESCE(w.probability, 0) AS win_probability,
  CASE
    WHEN w.probability > 0 THEN 650::float8 / 1073741824 / w.probability
    ELSE 0
  END AS gigabytes
FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
LEFT JOIN {{> win-probability}} AS w
  ON r.block >= w.from_block AND r.block < w.to_block
ORDER BY r.block, r.tx_index, r.log_index

queries.title: Client deployments
queries.description: Every VPN client deployment, by block, newest first.
queries.sql:
-- Every VPN client deployment (vpn-clients), newest first: the block its key
-- binding was made in.
SELECT
  deployed_block AS block,
  {{> hex(client)}} AS client,
  {{> indexed-block}} AS head_block
FROM {{> vpn-clients}} AS clients
ORDER BY deployed_block DESC, account_id DESC

queries.title: uint256
queries.description: Expression fragment: a 32-byte big-endian integer as an exact numeric. {{> uint256(balance)}}.
queries.sql:
-- An unsigned big-endian integer of up to 32 bytes — how Blokli stores token
-- amounts — as an exact numeric. Read four bytes at a time, since no integer
-- type holds 256 bits.
--
--   {{> uint256(balance)}}   →   171260453116000000000000
(
  SELECT SUM(
    ('x' || SUBSTRING(LPAD(encode({{$value = '\x0de0b6b3a7640000'::bytea}}, 'hex'), 64, '0') FROM 8 * i + 1 FOR 8))::bit(32)::bigint::numeric
    * (4294967296::numeric ^ (7 - i))
  )
  FROM generate_series(0, 7) AS i
)

queries.title: Network state
queries.description: Accounts, safes, open channels and their balance at the last indexed block, from the event log.
queries.sql:
-- The network as it stands at the last indexed block: one row.
--
-- All but the block is read from the event log: accounts from their key
-- bindings, safes from the stake factory's NewHoprNodeStakeModuleForSafe
-- (address module, address safe) — the safe is data word 1 — and each channel
-- as its latest event left it. Balances are wei, as exact numerics.
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (e.channel_id) e.status, e.balance
  FROM {{> channel-events}} AS e
  ORDER BY e.channel_id, e.block_number DESC, e.tx_index DESC, e.log_index DESC
),
open_channel AS (
  SELECT {{> uint256(balance)}} AS wei FROM latest WHERE status = 1
),
head AS (
  SELECT {{> indexed-block}} AS indexed_block
)
SELECT
  head.indexed_block,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {{> key-bindings}} AS account) AS accounts,
  (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SUBSTRING(data FROM 45 FOR 20))
    FROM {{> event-logs(ARRAY['\x83a5c31bfee49d254d95e3946d8e8434e5975382fa8b849182db9e251aaaaa26'::bytea])}} AS e
    WHERE OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 64
  ) AS safes,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM open_channel) AS open_channels,
  COALESCE((SELECT ROUND(SUM(wei)) FROM open_channel), 0) AS channel_balance
FROM head

queries.title: Ticket parameters
queries.description: Current winning probability, ticket price and ticket value.
queries.sql:
-- The oracle values as they stand: winning probability, ticket price, and
-- what a ticket is worth for one remaining hop (price ÷ probability). One row.
--
-- The newest update of each in {{> oracle-updates}}, so the figures match the
-- history the volume is priced with; both are null when the oracle has never
-- been indexed. Per network only: each network sets its own price and
-- probability, so a combined figure would be a fiction.
WITH latest_probability AS (
  SELECT {{> decode-win-prob(value)}} AS value
  FROM {{> oracle-updates}} AS oracle
  WHERE kind = 'win-prob'
  ORDER BY block_number DESC, tx_index DESC, log_index DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
latest_price AS (
  SELECT {{> uint256(value)}} AS wei
  FROM {{> oracle-updates}} AS oracle
  WHERE kind = 'ticket-price'
  ORDER BY block_number DESC, tx_index DESC, log_index DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  (SELECT value FROM latest_probability) AS win_probability,
  (SELECT ROUND(wei) FROM latest_price) AS ticket_price,
  (
    SELECT ROUND(latest_price.wei / latest_probability.value::numeric)
    FROM latest_price, latest_probability
    WHERE latest_probability.value > 0
  ) AS ticket_value

queries.title: Exits
queries.description: The network’s Gnosis VPN exits, where each is reached and the downstream volume it paid.
queries.sql:
-- Every exit the dashboard knows, with the downstream volume it paid for.
--
-- The exits are those of exit-addresses, found in the service registry, the
-- list "exits" or both. For a registered exit, the registry also says its name
-- and where it is reached (the VPN server and the WireGuard server of its
-- metadata) and which safe registered it. Volume is what the exit paid relays
-- for the return path, all time, priced at the winning probability in force at
-- each block as in vpn-traffic; an exit that never paid a relay has none.
WITH registered AS MATERIALIZED {{> registry-entries}},
traffic AS (
  SELECT
    r.payer,
    COUNT(*) AS redemptions,
    MAX(r.block) AS last_active_block,
    SUM(CASE WHEN w.probability > 0 THEN 650::float8 / 1073741824 / w.probability ELSE 0 END) AS gigabytes
  FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
  LEFT JOIN {{> win-probability}} AS w
    ON r.block >= w.from_block AND r.block < w.to_block
  WHERE r.direction = 'downstream'
  GROUP BY r.payer
)
SELECT
  reg.name,
  {{> hex(x.address)}} AS exit,
  CASE
    WHEN x.in_registry AND x.in_list THEN 'registry and list'
    WHEN x.in_registry THEN 'registry'
    ELSE 'list'
  END AS found_in,
  reg.vpn_server,
  reg.wireguard_server,
  {{> hex(reg.safe)}} AS safe,
  COALESCE(t.gigabytes, 0) AS gigabytes,
  COALESCE(t.redemptions, 0) AS redemptions,
  t.last_active_block
FROM {{> exit-addresses}} AS x
LEFT JOIN registered AS reg ON reg.address = x.address
LEFT JOIN traffic AS t ON t.payer = x.address
ORDER BY gigabytes DESC, exit

queries.title: Recent redemptions
queries.description: The 500 most recent client redemptions, with their channel.
queries.sql:
-- The 500 most recent client redemptions, with the channel they were on.
--
-- The same population as the upstream rows of vpn-traffic — a client paying
-- an announced relay — but read newest first and capped, because it is the
-- only result that needs the channel id, and carrying a 64-character id on
-- every row of the full history would cost far more than this feed shows.
SELECT
  r.block,
  {{> hex(r.payer)}} AS client,
  {{> hex(r.relay)}} AS relay,
  '0x' || r.channel AS channel,
  r.tickets
FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
WHERE r.direction = 'upstream'
ORDER BY r.block DESC, r.tx_index DESC, r.log_index DESC
LIMIT 500

queries.title: Indexed contracts
queries.description: The contracts this index subscribes to, by role.
queries.sql:
-- The contracts this index subscribes to, named by the events they emit.
--
-- Blokli records one row per (contract, event topic) it watches, so the
-- distinct addresses are the contracts indexed and the topics — 32-byte event
-- signature hashes — say what each one is.
WITH contract AS (
  SELECT address, ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT encode(topic, 'hex') ORDER BY encode(topic, 'hex')) AS topics
  FROM log_topic_info
  GROUP BY address
)
SELECT
  {{> hex(contract.address)}} AS contract
FROM contract
ORDER BY contract
